extraction.name: Vibravox
extraction.description: A GDPR-compliant dataset of French speech captured with five body-conduction audio sensors plus an airborne reference microphone. It contains about 45 hours per sensor from 188 participants recorded under different acoustic conditions, with recording-condition annotations and linguistic transcriptions.
extraction.creator: Julien Hauret, Malo Olivier, Thomas Joubaud, Christophe Langrenne, Sarah Poirée, Véronique Zimpfer, and Éric Bavu
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The section indicates the dataset was created through experimental recordings, including a 3D sound spatialization system used during recording, and mentions limited training data with additional synthetic data.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Recorded speech data, including emotional bone conducted speech, throat and acoustic paired speech, and synthetic data used alongside a limited training set.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Linguistic transcriptions and phonetic transcriptions were created from normalized French Wikipedia/Common Voice text using the CoML lab phonemizer, with manual phonetic transcription for unrecognized words; annotation quality was further controlled by automatic post-processing filters using Whisper-based phoneme error rate and signal quality criteria.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Annotation quality was analyzed with automatic filtering based on phoneme error rate (PER) computed via Levenshtein distance between labeled and Whisper-derived phonetic transcriptions, plus signal-quality checks (SNR and speech-vs-silence level thresholds). Samples with PER > 10% or poor signal quality were discarded.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: CoML lab text phonemizer; whisper-timestamped model based on Whisper with dynamic time warping for timestamp alignment and phonetic/transcription-based filtering.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset creators attempted to reduce demographic bias by recruiting a diverse and gender-balanced participant group to improve representativeness and inclusivity.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset showed task-dependent performance limitations: while useful for speech enhancement and phoneme transcription, enhancement was found to hurt speaker verification performance.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to advance body-conducted speech analysis and enable more robust communication systems for real-world applications.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Gender information is implicated, as the participant recruitment explicitly aimed for a gender-balanced group.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is publicly released for speech processing tasks including speech enhancement, speech-to-phonemes, and speaker verification.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The corpus is publicly available online on HuggingFace under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International license.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The dataset was post-filtered to remove low-quality utterances using automatic filters based on pronunciation accuracy and signal quality, then split by speaker into train/validation/test with 80/10/10 male and female speakers.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Audio acquisition applied a uniform 20 Hz high-pass filter to each channel. Text data were filtered to remove problematic utterances (e.g., proper names, numbers, Greek letters, mathematical symbols, syntactic errors), then normalized by lowercasing and removing punctuation except apostrophes. Phonetic transcriptions were generated with a phonemizer, with some manual corrections for unrecognized words. After filtering accepted samples, VAD timestamps were extended by 0.6 s on both sides and trimmed by 15 ms at boundaries when needed.

name.evidence: Vibravox: A Dataset of French Speech Captured with Body-conduction Audio Sensors

description.evidence: Abstract —Vibravox is a dataset compliant with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) containing audio recordings using five different body-conduction audio sensors... The Vibravox corpus contains 45 hours per sensor of speech samples and physiological sounds recorded by 188 participants under different acoustic conditions... Annotations about the recording conditions and linguistic transcriptions are also included in the corpus.
